still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates. Oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there, and maintenance pills still cost $199.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived. Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% adherence-tied premium differentials still stands. Illinois's ban is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 34.4% ever-used − 23.7% current = 10.7% of adults off now (2.8 pts cycled and off again plus 7.9 pts who stopped once and never restarted). About 50% of current users are on a second or later course (11.85 pts), so (11.85 + 2.8) / 34.4 ≈ 42.6% of ever-users have cycled. The share fell from 45% because the 5.6 pts of new ever-users are mostly first-course, low-dose wellness starters with fewer GI dropouts. Age check: 0.20×13 + 0.33×24 + 0.24×35.5 + 0.23×20.5 = 2.6 + 7.9 + 8.5 + 4.7 ≈ 23.7. Income thirds average ~23.7. 23.7% of ~274M adults ≈ 64.9M users, up ~11.6M. Payer mix: commercial ~14.2M (21.9%), Medicare ~12.4M (19.1%), Medicaid ~3.3M (5.1%), legitimate cash (TrumpRx, direct, telehealth) ~26.5M (40.8%), imported or counterfeit ~8.5M (13.1%); sum 64.9M. Users who started without obesity (BMI <30) number ~10.5M, ~16% of users: ~6.3M on 'metabolic health'/longevity protocols, ~2.4M on calm/focus plans, ~1.8M on alcohol or other off-label use. Nearly all pay cash and skew top-third and 45–70. They account for most of the top third's rise (25 → 31). Adult obesity is ~32.8%. About 22% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without CVD codes. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s are on a drug (12–17s ~2.5%, 6–11s ~0.2% on liraglutide). New prepubertal starts stayed low after the 2032 communication. About 5.0M children live with a parent who regained after stopping, and roughly 3M more live in a household where a parent of normal weight takes a drug 'for health'.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~12.4M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity + established CVD) codes behind prior authorisation, unchanged in structure. It grew by people ageing into codes. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 12.4M × ~$235 average net/month (flat; the price drift stopped) × 12 ≈ $35.0B a year gross Part D incretin spend. Dementia route ~2.1M × ~$245 × 12 ≈ $6.2B. Medicaid: the same 7 states cover weight-loss use, and ~3.3M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Longevity and calm use is never publicly covered.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 120+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $18–55. Canadian and Brazilian generics are steady at CAD 50–85 and BRL 180–300. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. No manufacturer cut a TrumpRx or direct price in 2033 or 2034: Wegovy pill starting $149 / maintenance $199, Foundayo $149–229, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299, MariTide direct $249, retatrutide ~$399 cash, amycretin $1,249 list. The stall has three causes. Oral semaglutide needs far more API per patient than injectables, and low-dose wellness fills now compete for that capacity. Volume growth removed the incentive to discount. No new launch forced a response. Commercial net prices were flat in 2033–34 after drifting down 3–5% a year. Employer coverage is still 30%, and ~12% more cover only through monitored tracks, which hold ~6.0M enrollees inside the ~14.2M commercial users. ~4.2M of them are on clinic MariTide (~5.1M MariTide users in total). Orals are ~50% of users, pushed up by low-dose wellness use. The gray market is ~8.5M users. The cash-to-Indian-generic gap widened to ~50–60× as Indian prices kept falling and US prices did not. Longevity clinics and telehealth 'metabolic' plans add $39–150 a month in platform or membership fees on top of the TrumpRx fill.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring label since Apr 2032)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; the confirmatory trial read out supportive in Dec 2033)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity protocols in adults without obesity: low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo through longevity clinics and telehealth, ~6.3M users
dementia-prevention use by 50–75-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid
alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs (the AUD sNDA got a CRL)

semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (rare since 2032)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached market, consistent with next_gen_launch none. The bimagrumab-type muscle adjunct (filed Jul 2032) received a CRL in Jun 2033: FDA wanted function and fracture outcomes, not lean mass alone. A new trial is under way and no approval is possible before 2036. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) received a CRL in Oct 2033 requesting a second adequate trial and a driving-impairment assessment, so AUD use stays off-label. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial in the obesity-plus-CVD population read out in Dec 2033 with a hazard ratio near 0.82. Lilly resubmitted the 60+ non-CVD extension in May 2034, with a decision due 2035. The longevity_wellness driver is realised entirely off-label, through prescriber discretion and existing low-dose products. Implant programmes are in phase 2 and not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. The global incretin market is ~$195B (2033). US net prices are flat, the first two-year pause since launch.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on standard doses. Low-dose wellness users report it less, which is part of why their persistence is higher. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is still worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Lower absolute rates in non-obese low-dose users, who lose less weight.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL proceeding, with the first bellwether trial set for 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 after 2+ years in 65+ users and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. No new signal. Exposure has widened as normal-weight 60–75-year-olds start longevity protocols without DXA baselines. Their risk at low dose is uncharacterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code in use; the muscle adjunct was refused (CRL Jun 2033).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (reported Oct 2033) put clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7% of users on standard doses vs ~3% of controls, and ~10% on retatrutide. These figures are consistent with earlier cohorts. The low-dose subgroup (n≈1,900) showed no significant excess but could not rule out a doubling. No randomised data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FDA called for a randomised low-dose study and did not require one. It sent untitled letters to two more platforms in 2034, and no enforcement followed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles and fastest in gray-market users after bad batches.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; fat-soluble deficiency tied to EPI; low ferritin in adolescent girls. Longevity clinics now sell panels as part of membership.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years), with partial recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. Tirzepatide's 5+ year excess remains small and non-significant. Longevity users who intend lifelong use are the group with the most future exposure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide EPI warning (Mar 2031) retained; tirzepatide still under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Decades-long low-dose use in healthy adults has never been studied prospectively. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas remain poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; no requirement covers off-label healthy-adult use.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000 by mid-2034. No cluster in 2033–34 matched the 2031 outbreaks, but sporadic mycobacterial and overdose cases continue. Cloned-serial pens persist, and poison-centre calls are ~5.5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained. CBP seizures are flat at the 2031 level, and personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update (2033) held at ~0.6–0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters, with early hints of catch-up in children who stopped. The Swedish registry findings stand. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Feb 2032 communication and Apr 2032 label retained. The EMA added similar monitoring language in 2033. No age restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~11–13% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~11%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down as premium mix stops offsetting volume. A new upper-income segment of normal-weight 'metabolic' users buys protein, fibre and 'longevity' SKUs; PepsiCo's and Mondelez's spun-off protein brands now chase them. A counter-niche grows around the Naturals: full-fat dairy, sourdough and butcher counters are up in Boise, Bozeman and parts of Brooklyn and Asheville. Kroger tests 'whole kitchen' endcaps beside the protein bays.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~15% from 2025 and beer ~10%. Longevity users drink less even without targeting, and calm plans bundle alcohol reduction. Wine clubs lose 45–65-year-old upper-income members. Bar closures continue in mid-sized Midwestern cities. Craft breweries in Naturals-heavy towns market 'unmedicated' taprooms.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down and portion tiers are standard. Fine dining sells 'tasting' menus for medicated diners alongside 'Natural tables' with family-style excess in a handful of cities. QSR value menus grow in lower-income markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Premium athletic and tailoring hold. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. The Naturals have a look of their own, workwear, wool and roomier cuts, sold by small Idaho and Montana brands and copied by Madewell-type chains.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. Longevity clinics bundle DXA, VO2max and low-dose prescriptions at $200–500 a month. Natural bodybuilding and powerlifting federations that test for incretins report record entries. Employer tracks keep InBody scans.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is unchanged at 30% and tracks hold 6.0M enrollees. Pharmacy trend is ~+7% now that net prices no longer fall. Insurers refuse longevity claims, and some life insurers ask applicants about non-indicated incretin use, without pricing it. Part D premiums rose again in 2033 and 2034.

pharma.state: Volume grows at flat prices, which is the best margin environment since launch. Novo's oral semaglutide is supply-allocated between indicated and low-dose fills. Lilly's dementia confirmatory readout revived growth. Amgen holds the employer tracks. Manufacturers decline to promote longevity use but report it in earnings as 'non-indicated wellness demand'.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape still reads as income and payment channel. A new reading: a normal-weight 55-year-old who is unusually lean and quiet is presumed to be 'on protocol'. Among the Naturals, a soft middle, flushed face and big appetite are worn on purpose as proof of not taking it.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the upper-tier uniform. In Austin and Charlotte the newest status is a low-dose longevity protocol in a body that never had obesity. The 'off-drug lean' boast has partly given way to 'never needed it, take it anyway'. The Columbus-corridor plant-clinic body and the Memphis cycler body persist. In Boise and surrounding Ada and Canyon counties, Naturals turn 'unmedicated' into a regional middle-class identity that is mostly white, church-adjacent and outdoorsy, with a smaller secular left wing in Brooklyn and Asheville.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter in medicated households. Naturals host 'whole table' suppers where the point is to eat a lot together, post the plates and wear the hunger. Bread Alone (~700 congregations) and the Naturals overlap in the Mountain West, even though one fasts and the other feasts. School-lunch debates are unchanged in law.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps carry three tags now: 'lean-mass verified', 'on a calm plan' and 'Natural'. The last is the fastest-growing filter in Idaho, Utah and Montana. Some Natural users ask for a home test strip result; a $29 urine semaglutide strip sold online is unvalidated. Couples therapists add a new mismatch: one partner joining a longevity protocol 'to live longer for you', the other hearing it as a bet against their shared life.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier appetite is a lever, tuned even in people who were never heavy. For Naturals it is a sign of being fully alive. Their slogan is 'Feel the whole thing.' In the bottom third appetite still mostly signals lost access. Unmuted and the Naturals share events but argue: Unmuted says access is a class question, while Naturals say the drug itself is the problem.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA observational study (Oct 2033) confirmed ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia on standard doses vs ~3% in controls, ~10% on retatrutide. The low-dose subgroup was underpowered: no significant excess, and a doubling was not ruled out. Calm and focus subscribers number ~2.4M. Longevity protocols (~6.3M) are mostly sold on metabolic markers, but intake forms and marketing increasingly mention 'steadier mood' as a side benefit. Telehealth platforms quote the low-dose null finding in their ads.
interior_life.framing: Platforms call it a feature: 'quiet', 'baseline', 'steady state'. Longevity clinics call it 'metabolic and emotional homeostasis'. Manufacturers still say 'food noise' and decline to comment on wellness use. Clinicians call it dose-related. Naturals call it 'the hush' and treat refusing it as identity.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~6.0M employees are in adherence-verified tracks, and shift-lead promotions on the Columbus corridor still informally favour enrollees. In finance and consulting in Charlotte and New York, a longevity protocol sits on the same wellness stipend line as sleep coaching. One 2032 EEOC charge was closed with a right-to-sue notice, and a former call-centre worker sued in federal court in Ohio in 2034; the case is pending. Some Boise-area small businesses advertise 'Natural-run'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir gives way to Natural maximalism: loud live music, food content about eating rather than portions, and comedians who name the drug in the first minute. The Naturals' signature sports are tested natural bodybuilding and amateur powerlifting. Calm-plan subscribers keep favouring ambient streaming. Sportsbook wagering per account keeps falling in insured suburbs.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The monthly shot date and the daily pill both organise couples' routines. Desire mismatch remains the top complaint at some practices. A new pattern: midlife couples where one starts a longevity protocol and the other reads the new evenness as distance.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No state acted. In the 2034 midterms a handful of Mountain West candidates campaigned as 'unmedicated' and two House challengers in Idaho and Utah won primaries partly on it. A Texas incumbent mentioned his longevity protocol in a podcast and was attacked for it. MAHA-aligned hearings continued on the children's data and longevity marketing without bills. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Medicated and Natural voters are increasingly sorted by county.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive. FDA issued CRLs on the muscle adjunct and on AUD, published the anhedonia observational study without labelling, accepted Lilly's dementia resubmission, and took no action on off-label longevity prescribing, which it treats as practice of medicine. Untitled letters went to platforms over explicit mood claims. No state law or rule changed.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx runs on manufacturer-set prices that have not moved since 2031. The Bridge pilot is not revived, and the 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. Clinic records, PBM fills and telehealth mood logs flow to wellness vendors under consent. Longevity clinics add biomarker dashboards that employers can sponsor. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Natural sports federations run incretin urine testing, the only routine incretin drug testing in the country, and it is private.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged and the Army oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT has still not ruled on off-label or calm-plan use among commercial drivers. The AUD CRL's driving-impairment request revived the question without resolving it.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply about two-thirds of world volume. Oral semaglutide API is the tightest input, and Novo has added contract capacity in the US and Denmark but not enough to cut price. US–India talks on mail enforcement are still without agreement, and the price gap is ~50–60×.

events.event: Novo Nordisk, Lilly and Amgen leave TrumpRx and direct cash prices unchanged for 2033, the first annual reset without a cut since 2026. Novo cites oral semaglutide API allocation as low-dose 'wellness' fills climb.

The largest US natural bodybuilding federation adds semaglutide, tirzepatide and other incretins to its banned list. Boise-based Naturals supper clubs pass 400 chapters and 'Natural' becomes a dating-app filter.

FDA's postmarketing observational study finds anhedonia at ~7% of standard-dose users vs ~3% of controls and no significant excess at low doses in an underpowered subgroup. No label change follows, and calm platforms quote the null in their ads.

Lilly's confirmatory trial supports tirzepatide's dementia-risk reduction in adults with obesity and heart disease. Longevity clinics cite it in marketing to healthy 50-year-olds before Lilly's May 2034 resubmission for the broader label.

Industry analysts estimate about 10 million Americans without obesity now take an incretin for 'metabolic health', longevity or calm, almost all paying cash for low-dose pills at the $149 TrumpRx starting price plus clinic fees.
Business Group on Health survey again finds 30% of employers covering weight-loss drugs, with monitored metabolic tracks at 6.0 million enrollees and no employer covering longevity use.

open_tensions: About 6.3 million normal-weight adults, many of them 60 to 75, take incretins indefinitely for longevity without DXA baselines. They belong to the group whose fracture and pancreatic risks drove the 2031 dementia CRL, and no trial covers them. Lilly's resubmission, due in 2035, could put that use on the label or confirm the warning.

Calm is a product with a null result printed on it. A low-dose subgroup that could not rule out a doubling of anhedonia now underwrites 2.4 million subscriptions and the mood language in longevity marketing. FDA asked for a randomised study and did not require one.

With US prices frozen and Indian generics still falling, the gap is 50–60×. 8.5 million people rely on mail and counterfeit product, and the bottom third's use remains the least stable in the country.

The Naturals turned not taking the drug into an identity with test strips, tested sports and candidates. Medicated and unmedicated America are now sorting by county and by dating filter, and the 2034 primaries suggest disclosure will become a political demand.

prose.headline: The Healthy Are Taking It Now: 10 Million Americans Without Obesity Are On It, and the Naturals Want You to Know They Aren't
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 nearly one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about sixty-five million people, and a third of adults have tried one. Adoption grew faster than in the previous two years, but not because anyone got cheaper access. Prices stopped falling. In January 2033 the three big makers left their cash prices where they had been since 2031: $149 for a starting Wegovy pill, $199 to maintain it, $249 for a monthly MariTide shot. They did the same again in 2034. The oral pill needs a great deal of active ingredient, and the factories that make it have a new kind of customer.

That customer is not overweight. About ten million Americans without obesity now take a low dose for what longevity clinics call metabolic health and telehealth platforms call baseline. They are mostly between forty-five and seventy, mostly in the top third of incomes, and almost all pay cash. The pill costs the same $149 as anyone's starting dose, and a clinic membership adds anything from $39 to several hundred dollars for the blood panels and body scans. No insurer pays for it, no label mentions it, and the FDA treats it as doctors' business. In December 2033 Lilly's trial confirmed that tirzepatide lowers dementia risk in heavy patients with heart disease. The clinics put the hazard ratio in their brochures before the company had even refiled for healthy older adults.

The calm market rode alongside. About 2.4 million people subscribe to plans that promise quiet and focus. In October 2033 the FDA's long-awaited study found that standard doses roughly double the rate of real anhedonia. At low doses it found nothing significant in a group too small to find much. The platforms now quote that sentence in their ads.

The structure of who pays stayed exactly where it was. Thirty percent of employers cover the drugs for weight loss, and six million workers get their monthly shot at the plant clinic with the record sent to a vendor. Medicare pays about $35 billion a year through the same narrow codes. Seven Medicaid programmes cover weight loss. Eight and a half million people buy by mail or from counterfeiters, because an Indian vial now costs a fiftieth of the American cash price and the American price no longer moves.

No new drug arrived. The FDA turned down a muscle-preserving companion drug and the alcohol indication, both for wanting better evidence. No new harm was found. The old ones stayed on the books: the fractures in older users, the pancreas after five years, slower growth in children who started young. Fewer children start now. Most of the new long-term exposure is in healthy sixty-year-olds.

The most visible change is a refusal. In Boise a few dinner clubs became four hundred chapters of people who call themselves Naturals. They eat a lot together, wear wool and soft middles, and say their slogan, 'Feel the whole thing', without irony. The largest natural bodybuilding federation now tests for incretins, the only routine incretin testing in the country. Dating apps added a Natural filter. In the 2034 primaries two Mountain West challengers ran as unmedicated and won. Nobody passed a law. Unmuted, the older movement, argues that access is the issue. The Naturals answer that the drug is.

So the country sorts by county. In Austin the prized body never needed the drug and takes it anyway. On the Columbus corridor it gets a shot every month from the clinic. In Memphis it cycles. In Boise it is proud of being hungry. Seen from outside, everyone looks fine.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Ruiz is sixty-one and has never weighed more than 160 pounds. She takes the pill at 6:10, before coffee, with four ounces of water exactly, the way the Baseline app's chime tells her. The fill came from TrumpRx: $149. Baseline charges $49 on top for the monthly video check and the panel. Her ferritin is fine, and the app gives it a green leaf.

She dispatches school buses for the Meridian district. At 7:40 route 14 is down a driver, and she reroutes two buses without raising her voice. Her supervisor says she's been a rock this year. She doesn't miss the old feeling of her pulse in her throat and doesn't think about it.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and throws the other half away.

Her daughter Kels picks her up because the Subaru is in the shop. Kels has a Natural sticker on the tailgate, a loaf of sourdough on the passenger seat and flour on her jeans. She doesn't ask about the pill. She asks whether Dana is coming to Thursday's supper at the Grange hall, where they roast two whole chickens and nobody leaves early.

'I eat like a bird now,' Dana says.

'You can just come and sit.'

At home Dana's husband watches a game with the sound low. He took a semaglutide pen for his heart until it moved to prior auth, and he quit in March. He has put twelve pounds back on. He laughs at something on the screen. Dana listens to him for a while, then goes to set the chime for tomorrow.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral semaglutide needs far more API per patient than injectables, and low-dose wellness fills now compete for that capacity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the stall is the stipulated driver, but its stated cause is backwards. Low-dose wellness fills use little API per patient, so they cannot plausibly squeeze supply enough to freeze every maker's cash price for two years.

Magnitude: 20.5% of about 63M adults 65+ is roughly 12.9M users, but Medicare alone is 12.4M. That leaves almost no room for the ~6.3M mostly cash-paying longevity users, many aged 60–75, so the age bands and payer mix do not fully reconcile.

least_plausible_claims.quote: two House challengers in Idaho and Utah won primaries partly on it
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a movement with a few hundred supper-club chapters is asserted to win federal primaries within about a year. No chain links the movement to electoral wins, and the attribution is unsupported.

rationale.badness: About 65M adults are on the drugs, including ~6.3M healthy 60–75-year-olds on indefinite low-dose protocols with no DXA baselines and uncharacterised fracture and EPI risk. The low-dose anhedonia null that cannot rule out a doubling is now used as ad copy. Stratification persists: 8.5M gray-market users, a 50–60× price gap, and the world sorting 'by county' into medicated and Natural. It is a harder society with new losers, but no structural catastrophe, and there is no new safety signal and no state action, which caps severity.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable. Price is frozen (event 2033-01), coverage is flat at 30%, longevity use is realised off-label, the Natural movement is present, safety signal and market shock are absent, and the personality layer is marketed. Approval timing obeys the envelope's rules. mechanism: the price stall rests on the API-allocation story (claim 1), which runs the wrong way for low-dose fills. The leap to ~6.3M longevity users and the Natural primary wins (claim 3) are partly asserted rather than shown. The husband 'moved to prior auth' line in the prose sits oddly with Medicare PA already being in place. magnitude: 23.7% on drug and 34.4% ever-used are inside the envelope, and payer mix, Medicare spend ($35.0B, dementia $6.2B), age and income checks and the cycled-share arithmetic all reconcile. The one gap is 65+ users against Medicare plus older longevity cash users (claim 2).
rationale.generativity: Dana Ruiz is a concrete scene-bearing character, with the chime, the $49 Baseline fee, the half-eaten wrap and the Natural daughter's supper invitation. Her husband's regain adds texture. The world supplies many implied scenes: Boise supper clubs, the urine test strip, the Columbus clinic shot and the Memphis cycler. The day-in-the-life mostly shows rather than explains.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral semaglutide needs far more API per patient than injectables, and low-dose wellness fills now compete for that capacity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: low-dose wellness pills use far less API per patient than the 25 mg maintenance pill. It is odd that ~10M low-dose users would be the thing that ends discounting, and the 'far more API' premise does not support that conclusion.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In the 2034 midterms a handful of Mountain West candidates campaigned as 'unmedicated' and two House challengers in Idaho and Utah won primaries partly on it.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a lifestyle identity that began after 2032 is shown winning federal primaries within two years. Nothing in the world shows the political vehicle, the electorate or the counts behind it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: He took a semaglutide pen for his heart until it moved to prior auth, and he quit in March.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world says coverage is status quo and Medicare CV codes were already behind prior authorisation in 2032. A cardiac user losing a pen because it 'moved to prior auth' contradicts the unchanged structure and is a narrative-world inconsistency.

The prose's 'six million workers get their monthly shot at the plant clinic' also overstates the 4.2M clinic-MariTide figure. magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope (23.7 current, 34.4 ever, income thirds bracket, age check ≈23.7). Only the pace of growth in non-obese users is steep.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral semaglutide needs far more API per patient than injectables, and low-dose wellness fills now compete for that capacity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the stall is the stipulated driver, but its stated cause is backwards. Low-dose wellness fills use little API per patient, so they cannot plausibly squeeze supply enough to freeze every maker's cash price for two years.

Magnitude: 20.5% of about 63M adults 65+ is roughly 12.9M users, but Medicare alone is 12.4M. That leaves almost no room for the ~6.3M mostly cash-paying longevity users, many aged 60–75, so the age bands and payer mix do not fully reconcile.
